Official website for JitForge — an enterprise-grade in-memory Java runtime compilation, JIT execution, and cloud-native bytecode synthesis engine built on Java 21 Loom Virtual Threads. JitForge enables organizations to compile, optimize, cache, and execute dynamic Java source code entirely in RAM with zero disk I/O, sub-millisecond caching, multi-tier dependency resolution, sandboxed security, and containerized microservice APIs.

🚀 Core Capabilities & System Architecture

⚡ In-Memory Compilation & Execution

Zero interface or base class constraints. Pass plain Java source code and let the engine infer AST definitions automatically. Reflection-free dynamic invocation in RAM with zero disk I/O.

💾 4-Tier Distributed Bytecode Storage

Chain-of-responsibility storage hierarchy: ClassLoader RAM (<1µs) → Redis Cache (<1ms) → Pod Local Volume (2-5ms) → PostgreSQL DB (5-15ms) with automated read-through cache warming.

⚙️ Multi-Engine JIT Ecosystem

Dynamic per-request compiler engine selection: JAVAC (standard in-memory), JANINO (<15ms embedded JIT), GROOVY (@CompileStatic), Byte Buddy (proxy synthesis), Javassist, and MVEL 2.

🌐 Cloud-Native REST Microservice

Java 21 Loom Virtual Threads for non-blocking high-density concurrency. Exposes REST endpoints (/api/compile, /api/execute, /api/bytecode, /api/classes, /api/tiers, /api/health) ready for Podman and Kubernetes.

🔒 AST Lexical Sandboxing & Security

SecurityPolicy & CodeSecurityValidator proactively inspect source tokens before compilation to block RCE, System.exit, forbidden reflection, and unsafe file/network I/O. SandboxedExecutor bounds execution times.

📦 URLClassLoader & Client Interop

Remote client JVMs load server-compiled bytecodes dynamically via standard Java URLClassLoader (GET /api/classes/), Base64 JSON payloads, or raw binary .class downloads over HTTP.

🏢 Enterprise Impact & Problems Solved

⚡ Zero Disk Footprint & Sub-Millisecond Execution

Traditional compilation writes temporary files to disk, creating I/O bottlenecks. JitForge executes 100% in RAM via MemoryFileManager and MemoryClassLoader, delivering microsecond LRU cache hits and sub-15ms JIT compilation with zero disk footprint.

💡 Dynamic Business Logic & Scripting

Replaces slow interpreted scripting engines with native compiled JVM bytecodes. Execute dynamic pricing rules, complex routing policies, and custom tenant workflows at full JVM speed with zero reflection overhead.

🔒 Enterprise Proactive RCE Defense

Allowing dynamic user code introduces severe RCE risks. JitForge proactively inspects source tokens before compilation (CodeSecurityValidator) to block forbidden APIs, reflection, and I/O, while SandboxedExecutor bounds execution runtime against infinite loops.

💾 Distributed Bytecode Caching Across Pods

Eliminates redundant recompilation across scaled container fleets. Bytecodes compiled on one pod are cached and shared across 4 distributed tiers (RAM → Redis → Pod Storage → PostgreSQL DB) with automated read-through upstream warming.

🚀 Organizational Adoption & Integration Paths

JitForge is engineered for effortless adoption across existing enterprise stacks without forcing architecture rewrites or proprietary framework dependencies:

1. Embedded Java Library

Add JitForge directly to your Gradle or Maven project as a standard JVM library with fluent builder APIs.

DynamicCompiler compiler = new InMemoryCompiler();
2. Spring Boot Auto-Config

Inject compiler beans automatically into your Spring services with zero boilerplate configuration.

@Autowired DynamicCompiler compiler;
3. Microservice Container Stack

Deploy as a standalone REST daemon in Podman, Docker, or Kubernetes using pre-built Helm charts.

helm install jitforge ./deploy/helm/jitforge
4. Polyglot Client SDKs

Compile and execute JVM bytecodes from non-Java services using zero-dependency Python and TypeScript SDKs.

Python: pip package | Node.js: npm package

💻 Public Java APIs & Programmatic Usage

Programmatic API examples demonstrating in-memory source compilation, multi-tier dependency resolution, and sandboxed execution:

☕ Java API — In-Memory Source Compilation & Reflection-Free Execution 
import io.github.ervivekumrao.jitforge.api.DynamicCompiler;
import io.github.ervivekumrao.jitforge.api.CompilationResult;
import io.github.ervivekumrao.jitforge.engine.InMemoryCompiler;

// Initialize in-memory compiler (Zero disk I/O)
DynamicCompiler compiler = new InMemoryCompiler();

// 1. Plain Java Source Code (Package & Class name inferred automatically)
String sourceCode = """
        package com.example.service;

        public class DiscountCalculator {
            public double calculateDiscount(double price, int loyaltyTier) {
                double discount = loyaltyTier > 3 ? 0.20 : 0.05;
                return price * (1.0 - discount);
            }
        }
        """;

// 2. Compile directly in RAM (< 15ms)
CompilationResult<Object> result = compiler.compile(sourceCode);

// 3. Dynamic Execution without Reflection Boilerplate
Object instance = result.newInstance();
Object finalPrice = result.invokeOn(instance, "calculateDiscount", 250.0, 4);

System.out.println("Final Discounted Price: $" + finalPrice);
// Output: Final Discounted Price: $200.0
💾 Java API — 4-Tier Bytecode Storage & Cross-Pod Dependency Resolution 
// Configure compiler with 4-Tier Storage Hierarchy
DynamicCompiler podCompiler = InMemoryCompiler.builder()
        .withRedis("redis-service", 6379)
        .withFileSystemStore(Path.of("/var/data/compiler/classes"))
        .withDatabase("jdbc:postgresql://db-service:5432/bytecodes", "user", "password")
        .build();

// Compile billing service — automatically resolves previously compiled UserAccount
// from RAM > Redis > Local Volume > PostgreSQL DB
String serviceCode = """
        package com.example.service;

        import com.example.entity.UserAccount;

        public class BillingService {
            public String processPayment(UserAccount account, double amount) {
                double remaining = account.getCredit() - amount;
                return "User " + account.getUserId() + " charged $" + amount + ". Remaining: $" + remaining;
            }
        }
        """;

CompilationResult<Object> billingResult = podCompiler.compile(serviceCode);
Class<?> accountClass = podCompiler.loadClass("com.example.entity.UserAccount");

Object account = accountClass.getConstructor(String.class, double.class).newInstance("USR-9901", 750.0);
Object billingService = billingResult.newInstance();

Object output = billingResult.invokeOn(billingService, "processPayment", account, 150.0);
// Result: "User USR-9901 charged $150.0. Remaining: $600.0"
🔒 Java API — Security Policy & Execution Timeout Protection 
import io.github.ervivekumrao.jitforge.security.SecurityPolicy;
import io.github.ervivekumrao.jitforge.security.SandboxedExecutor;

// 1. Strict Security Policy (Blocks RCE, ProcessBuilder, System.exit, forbidden reflection)
SecurityPolicy policy = SecurityPolicy.builder()
        .blockImport("java.net")
        .blockImport("java.io")
        .blockPattern("System.exit")
        .maxSourceLength(50_000)
        .enforceSandbox(true)
        .build();

DynamicCompiler secureCompiler = new InMemoryCompiler(policy, null, null);

// 2. Execution Timeout Safeguard (Protects against infinite loops & thread hangs)
SandboxedExecutor executor = new SandboxedExecutor(Duration.ofSeconds(2));
Object outcome = executor.execute(() -> result.invokeOn(instance, "calculateDiscount", 100.0, 1));

🌐 Public REST Microservice APIs

JitForge exposes clean HTTP REST endpoints for containerized and polyglot application environments:

HTTP Method & Endpoint Purpose & Description Payload / Parameters
POST /api/compile Compiles Java source code in RAM and returns compilation status JSON: {"compiler":"JANINO","sourceCode":"..."}
POST /api/execute Instantiates and executes a compiled class method on the server JSON: {"className":"...","methodName":"...","args":[...]}
GET /api/bytecode/{className} Downloads raw compiled binary .class bytecode or Base64 payload Path Parameter: FQN Class Name
GET /api/classes/* Standard Java URLClassLoader endpoint for streaming bytecodes over HTTP HTTP GET Stream URL
GET /api/tiers Inspects 4-tier storage metrics, hit ratios, and active tier configurations None
GET /api/health Kubernetes / Podman liveness, readiness, and service status probe None
GET /metrics Prometheus OpenMetrics endpoint for cluster monitoring & Grafana dashboards None
🌐 REST API — cURL Microservice Interaction 
# 1. Compile Source Code via HTTP REST API
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/compile \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "compiler": "JANINO",
    "sourceCode": "package com.demo; public class TaxEngine { public double tax(double amt) { return amt * 0.18; } }"
  }'

# 2. Execute Method Dynamically
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "className": "com.demo.TaxEngine",
    "methodName": "tax",
    "args": ["500.0"]
  }'

# Response: {"status":"SUCCESS","result":90.0,"executionTimeMs":1.2}

⚙️ Available Configuration & Enterprise Knobs

JitForge adheres to 12-Factor app configuration principles. All knobs can be set via YAML, environment variables, or JVM properties:

Property / Setting Environment Variable Default Value Description
server.port JITFORGE_PORT 8080 HTTP microservice listening port
compiler.default-engine JITFORGE_COMPILER_ENGINE JAVAC Default JIT engine (JAVAC, JANINO, GROOVY)
store.redis.host REDIS_HOST localhost Redis Tier 2 bytecode cache host
store.database.url DATABASE_URL jdbc:postgresql://... PostgreSQL / SQL Tier 4 bytecode store JDBC URL
hash.algorithm JITFORGE_HASH_ALGORITHM SHA-256 Centralized cryptographic hashing digest algorithm
security.sandbox.timeout JITFORGE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT 5000ms SandboxedExecutor maximum thread execution threshold
⚙️ Enterprise YAML Configuration — deploy/jitforge.yaml 
server:
  port: 8080
  threads: loom # Java 21 Virtual Threads

compiler:
  default-engine: JAVAC
  lru-cache-size: 1000
  allow-reflection: false

store:
  tiers: [RAM, REDIS, FILESYSTEM, DATABASE]
  redis:
    host: "redis-service"
    port: 6379
  filesystem:
    path: "/var/data/compiler/classes"
  database:
    url: "jdbc:postgresql://db-service:5432/bytecodes"
    user: "${DB_USER}"
    password: "${DB_PASSWORD}"

security:
  strict-mode: true
  max-source-bytes: 1048576 # 1 MB limit
  execution-timeout-ms: 2000
